newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia farms to get new machines by end July - paper.
newsitem.headline: Serbia farms to get new machines by end July - paper.

text.p: All 7,000 agricultural machines and various equipment contracted by Serbia's Commodity Reserve Agency under a programme to revitalise the farm sector will be delivered by end-July, Belgrade daily Politika said on Tuesday.

Farmers and agricultural firms have so far received more than 30 percent of the contracted machinery and equipment through the Commodity Reserve Agency, Agency official Miroslav Ivic was quoted by the paper as saying.

Under contracts with the Agency, some 20 local manufacturers are to deliver 2,200 tractors, 150 grain combines, 220 maize harvesters, 400 wheat sowers and 50 various kinds of machines and auxiliary equipment to farmers and agricultural firms by the end of July, the report said.

As part of the programme to revive production in the metals complex and deliver machinery and equipment to agricultural producers, the Serbian government has secured 205 million dinars under favourable conditions, including barter.
On the basis of deliveries so far, producers are mostly offering wheat, maize, potatoes and calves in exchange for the machinery, Ivic said.
The plan adopted in April provides for the exchange of machinery for 16 agricultural products through contracts concluded between the Agency and some 200 authorised companies throughout Serbia.
According to some estimates, the country has around 400,000 tractors, 250,000 multi-cultivators and 24,000 combines and harvesters. The average age of combines and harvesters is 11-1/2 years.
